claims.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
claims.evidence: The scan marks exactly the descent bottoms. If their values in scan order are d_1,...,d_k, successive MoveToFront operations leave them as d_k,...,d_1. Removing and reinserting them never changes the relative order of unmarked entries. The closed formula also matched the literal algorithm on every permutation of lengths 0 through 9.
claims.witness: For arbitrary p, the final marked prefix is the reverse of the marked scan sequence, followed by the original unmarked subsequence.
claims.search_method: Direct operational proof plus exhaustive comparison of literal and closed-form implementations on 409114 permutation words.

claims.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
claims.evidence: The maximum i is unmarked, the first entry of nonempty R is marked because it follows i, and a later r_j remains to the right of i exactly when r_{j-1}<r_j. Thus the next right word is exactly A(R), independently of L. Iteration gives A^t(R), and i occupies position i exactly when that word becomes empty. A strictly shortens every nonempty word, so the minimum is well-defined.
claims.witness: After one round, right_of_i(T(L i R))=A(R); induction gives right_of_i(T^t(L i R))=A^t(R) throughout the phase.
claims.search_method: Symbolic one-round derivation, induction over rounds, and exhaustive checking of all induced phases through n=9.

claims.claim: Let B_0 be empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m). If q(m)=floor((sqrt(8m+1)-1)/2), then h(B_m)=q(m). For m>=2, B_m begins with m and the word to its right also has extinction time q(m).
claims.evidence: Associate each entry with its first greater entry to the right. A deletes precisely the leaves of this forest, preserving the induced forest on survivors, so h is its height. The decreasing-stack recurrence computes this height. The draft's explicit stack-signature induction for m=q(q+1)/2+r has maximum label q and handles the triangular-boundary transitions correctly, with m=0,1 as direct bases. Finally B_m=mR_m and m exceeds every entry of R_m, hence A(B_m)=A(R_m); for m>=2, h(B_m)=1+h(A(R_m))=h(R_m).
claims.witness: B_6=(6,3,1,2,5,4), whose A-iterates are (2,5),(5),empty, so both B_6 and its tail have height 3=q(6).
claims.search_method: Forest/stack proof audit; exact full stack signatures checked for m=1 through 2000, stack heights for m=0 through 2000, and literal repeated A-deletion for m=0 through 300.

claims.claim: For i>=2, a phase for active maximum i has its maximum possible length i-1 if and only if its active prefix is exactly (i,1,2,...,i-1).
claims.evidence: For active prefix L i R, the phase length is h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. Equality forces L empty and |A(R)|=|R|-1; the latter holds exactly when every adjacent pair of R is increasing. Since R then contains 1,...,i-1, it must equal (1,2,...,i-1). Conversely, A removes exactly the first entry from that increasing word each round, giving length i-1.
claims.witness: The equality chain h(R)=|R|=i-1 forces R=(1,2,...,i-1), and this word attains equality.
claims.search_method: Equality-case analysis plus exhaustive testing of every phase start induced by permutations through n=9.

claims.claim: If ell_i denotes the phase length for active maximum i, then ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=2i-4 for every i>=5.
claims.evidence: If ell_i<=i-2, adding ell_{i-1}<=i-2 proves the bound. Otherwise claim 3 forces the phase start (i,1,...,i-1). Direct induction gives T^t(i,1,...,i-1)=B_t,i,t+1,...,i-1, so the next phase starts at B_{i-1},i and has ell_{i-1}=q(i-1). For i>=5, q(i-1)<=i-3, because q(i-1)>=i-2 would imply (i-2)(i-1)/2<=i-1 and hence i<=4. Thus the sum is at most 2i-4.
claims.witness: The only exceptional case ell_i=i-1 ends at B_{i-1},i and contributes (i-1)+q(i-1)<=(i-1)+(i-3).
claims.search_method: Complete two-case proof, exact checking of the special-state identity through i=150, and exhaustive phase-pair testing through n=9.

claims.claim: For n>=5, W(n)<=n(n-1)/2-floor((n-3)/2). Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
claims.evidence: The individual caps sum to n(n-1)/2. Pairing phases as (n,n-1),(n-2,n-3),... with larger index at least 5 produces exactly floor((n-3)/2) disjoint pairs. Claim 4 saves at least one from the separate cap for every such pair, proving the displayed bound. This is O(n^2), which rules out any omega(n^2) round family.
claims.witness: Each pair headed by i improves its separate cap 2i-3 to 2i-4; summing the disjoint savings yields floor((n-3)/2).
claims.search_method: Symbolic summation with endpoint and parity checks; the resulting bound was also checked against the exhaustive maxima for n=5 through 9.
